title: Breathing a Different Air
subtitle: The skies are clear, no signs of rain.

items.text: Vortex Train
A Maglev train glides along a thin track, feeling almost as if it were weaving through the air. Within the carriage of the Vortex, passengers converse among themselves in hushed tones.

items.speaker: Scientist I
items.text: In other words, this material would function something like a fire ant colony crossing a river, fluidly replacing worn-out and damaged sections.

items.speaker: Scientist I
items.text: Each component hard-wired to preserve its collective superstructure ... resistant even to the erosion of time itself.
Mesmer Jr. looks around in astonishment, out the window, at the mountains rushing past, and then at the two passengers sitting across from her.

items.speaker: Mesmer Jr.
items.text: That jacket you're wearing ... Is that also the machine's doing?

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Yes, sometimes the interferometer automatically modifies our clothes to help us blend in with the world we've entered.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Though it looks like the machine decided that you and X already pass for normal here.
The neighboring passengers, having reached the end of their conversation, rise from their seats.
Passing by with wine glasses in hand, they join another group of scientists chatting at the end of the carriage.

items.speaker: Scientist I
items.text: We're currently at least 40 meters from the ground.

items.speaker: Scientist II
items.text: A conservative estimate, Comrade Paukov. I should say we are at least the height of a Vostok-K rocket off the ground, and that's if we include Comrade Gagarin standing on the module.

items.speaker: Alexei
items.text: Cracking jokes as always, comrade.
A hovering robot whizzes over X's head with a glass of wine and stops next to a scientist. It dutifully places the glass down and then zips back.

items.speaker: X
items.text: I have to say, it's an unusual circumstance when being dressed as a Laplace researcher renders someone more inconspicuous.
Beyond the windows of the train, countless hovering machines dot the skyline, hurrying to and fro along preset routes.
As the last few mountains blur past, the view outside opens up into a wide plain.

items.speaker: Mesmer Jr.
items.text: Those fields look endless.
Waves of gold span across the fertile plain, stretching far away into the horizon.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: It seems so peaceful.
Under the blazing sunlight, Mesmer Jr. spies a few black dots among the wheat.

items.speaker: Mesmer Jr.
items.text: Oh, they even appear to have farming robots.
There's a drone spraying some kind of liquid onto the field, followed closely by a doorframe-shaped machine tending to the crops.

items.speaker: X
items.text: I think there are some scientists down there as well. Could be some kind of agricultural experiment.
Pardon my interruption, comrades, but this is only a regular field.

items.speaker: Maxim
items.text: The three of them turn with a start to see an unfamiliar man standing beside them. He doesn't seem to register their surprise as he continues nonchalantly.
Those people down there in white next to the robots, they're simply farmers.
Well, I say "farmers," but in truth they are scientists too. Another marvel of Soviet ingenuity.
Our innovations in agricultural robotics have eliminated the more laborious and time-consuming aspects of farmwork.
Now these farmers can use their time researching new scientific advancements, which feeds back into further developments in food production.
And it's not just agriculture. Every industry has seen the benefits of Soviet innovation. That is why they say our way of life here is the best in all the world.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Thank you for the information. I don't suppose we've been introduced, have we?

items.speaker: Maxim
items.text: My apologies. Call me Maxim. I'm a journalist.

items.speaker: Maxim
items.text: And the three of you must be Doctors Vertin, X, and Mesmer Jr.; am I correct?

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Very much so. How do you know about us?

items.speaker: Maxim
items.text: The news of a young yet highly accomplished trio of scientists attending this year's International Polymer Summit has caught everyone's attention.

items.speaker: Maxim
items.text: It doesn't take a genius to see you three are the only ones on this train that fit the description. Saying all that, I'd be grateful if you would allow me an interview.
The young visitors exchange glances. Finally, X speaks.

items.speaker: X
items.text: Certainly. As it happens, we could really use someone who could introduce this place to us. We don't know much about where we're going or what's been happening here in the Soviet Union.

items.speaker: Maxim
items.text: That much is clear. Where should I start? Oh, of course, let's start with Kollektiv.

items.speaker: Maxim
items.text: All the robots you see are controlled by the Kollektiv Neural Network, which ensures their labor is never wasted.

items.speaker: Maxim
items.text: Who would've thought that robots would become our closest companions? Honest, stable, graceful, calm. They give each and every comrade their undivided attention.

items.speaker: Maxim
items.text: With these robots as our foundation, Soviet society began to progress at a relentless pace: maximizing production, removing oppression, increasing everyone's leisure time. A true utopia!

items.speaker: Maxim
items.text: Everyone's so happy, too happy. It seems almost as if we've forgotten the utter misery we went through not so long ago.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: You mean ...

items.speaker: Maxim
items.text: The Plague, yes. So many of us today choose to focus on our happiness and the bright future ahead. It's as though we've already forgotten about them—

items.speaker: Maxim
items.text: The ones who delivered us from those dark times, those who experienced true misery yet strove to lift us into this new age—they aren't here to enjoy any of this. Is that fair?
The young visitors glance at each other, apologetic looks on their faces.

items.speaker: Maxim
items.text: Forgive me. I'm dwelling on old wounds. You're at the age where you should be enjoying yourselves, not revisiting the tragedies of the past.
Maxim attempts to regain his composure as he shifts the topic.

items.speaker: Maxim
items.text: Now, a question for you young scientists: tell me, are robots as commonplace in your country as they are here?

items.speaker: X
items.text: That may be dependent on your definition of "robot," but I've worked with an animated hunk of metal before.
And a vial of thinking ferrofluid
items.edge_label: 还有会思考的瓶中帆船

items.text: And a talking ship in a bottle
items.edge_label: 还有会思考的瓶中帆船

items.speaker: Maxim
items.text: Is that so? Fascinating. Em, here I thought I'd been keeping up to date with the latest in foreign developments. Science develops by leaps and bounds every day, it seems.

items.speaker: Maxim
items.text: Ah, well. I suppose it's a sign of progress.

items.speaker: X
items.text: One of the "robots" I mentioned was once in charge of running our entire organization. She was obsessive about maintaining a full charge. We ended up placing charging stations for her all around our facilities.

items.speaker: X
items.text: But I don't see anything like that here.

items.speaker: Maxim
items.text: Does that mean you don't have access to Dr. Sechenov's polymer in your country? It was revolutionary here. People say it saved our entire way of life.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Polymer?

items.speaker: Maxim
items.text: Simply put, it's a programmable liquid material.

items.speaker: Maxim
items.text: It's the primary topic of the summit. I'm certain you'll come to fully understand everything about it once you arrive.

items.speaker: Maxim
items.text: And of course, you'll get to see another of Dr. Sechenov's "prized inventions"—the Twins.

items.speaker: X
items.text: I get the feeling you don't share their enthusiasm.

items.speaker: Maxim
items.text: Oh, I did not mean to imply anything negative.

items.speaker: Maxim
items.text: I should learn to watch my tongue. I fear my lack of expertise may end up confusing you.

items.speaker: Maxim
items.text: We will soon arrive at the summit. I advise you to take the opportunity to experience our country's scientific achievements for yourselves.

items.speaker: Maxim
items.text: But to answer your question, Dr. Sechenov's team developed a kind of functional hydrogen cell—stable fusion reactors in a polymer casing. That is what allows the robots to function without constant recharging.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: That sounds like the perfect gift for someone we know.

items.speaker: Vortex
items.text: Attention, passengers. The train is now arriving at its final stop. Please collect your vehicle activation code from Rafik, and a Turbine will transport you directly to the site of the International Polymer Summit.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Rafik?

items.speaker: Maxim
items.text: That would be the robot bartender. Don't worry. Just follow me.

items.speaker: Vortex
items.text: Please alight the train in an orderly fashion. We hope to see you again soon aboard the Vortex.
The Maglev train comes to a steady stop. As the young visitors follow the crowd of scientists moving toward the exit, they spot someone struggling to stay upright in the queue.

items.speaker: Mesmer Jr.
items.text: Is that scientist drunk?
In front of them, there's a scientist slumped against his friend. His eyes are unfocused, and his words slur together.

items.speaker: Ethan Brown
items.text: Kids? Why are these kids here? How old are you?

items.speaker: Ethan Brown
items.text: No one told me we could bring our families to the summit. Or did we get on the wrong train, and now we're headed to a Young Pioneer's camp?

items.speaker: Alexei
items.text: Comrade, I think these young people are scientists like us.

items.speaker: Ethan Brown
items.text: Scientists? Them? Apurrhahaha ...

items.speaker: Mesmer Jr.
items.text: At least we had the good sense not to drink ourselves silly before an important conference.

items.speaker: Ethan Brown
items.text: Young people these days, always in a rush. You should be at home enjoying the summer, playing on the swings ...

items.speaker: Alexei
items.text: You're being impolite. Our companions are waiting outside. Come with me!
He cuts off the rest of the man's ramblings and stumbles toward the exit while supporting his drunken friend.
X runs up to them with an apple in his hand.

items.speaker: X
items.text: Hold on. Why don't you have some fruit? He looks like he could use it.

items.speaker: Alexei
items.text: Th-Thank you. I'm sorry for his behavior.
The scientist picks up his pace in dragging his colleague away from the embarrassing scene.

items.speaker: Mesmer Jr.
items.text: Alcohol can have medicinal benefits in proper dosages.
Maxim furrows his brows, visible frustration on his face. He pats X on the shoulder.

items.speaker: Maxim
items.text: Don't take any of that to heart, friends. Next stop, the exhibition hall, and welcome to Facility 3826!

items.speaker: Maxim
items.text: This way. That's Rafik, the one in charge of the activation codes.
As Maxim approaches, the robot's optic sensors begin blinking rapidly, mimicking a human's skeptical squint.

items.speaker: Rafik
items.text: Requisition approved. Here's your vehicle activation code. Have a safe trip.
Maxim leaves them with a wave. Rafik turns to the young visitors and starts scanning them for identification.

items.speaker: Mesmer Jr.
items.text: Wait, our identities ...

items.speaker: X
items.text: Nothing to perspire over. We won't need any scanning, Rafik. I've already got a key.
X waves his hand, dismissing the robot's scanning eyes. Then, in a flash, he produces a vehicle activation key from his pocket.

items.speaker: Mesmer Jr.
items.text: Where did you get that?

items.speaker: X
items.text: It always pays to be prepared and to keep your eye sharp. This is the International Polymer Summit after all.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: I assume that means you took it from someone else?

items.speaker: Mesmer Jr.
items.text: Wait, when you gave them that fruit, did you ...

items.speaker: X
items.text: Shhh. All I did was facilitate a hands-on experience in the importance of politeness.

items.speaker: Rafik
items.text: Goodbye. Please have a safe trip.

items.speaker: Turbine
items.text: Please secure your seat belt. We wish you a very pleasant journey!
Six steel cables shoot out from the Bumblebee and attach to the Turbine, lifting the vehicle into the air.

items.speaker: X
items.text: If I'm not mistaken, our conference venue is on some kind of floating island. Fascinating.

items.speaker: X
items.text: Come on. Why don't we check out some of the local music!

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: This place really is like what the prediction indicated—a world that champions science, rationality, and order. Wouldn't you agree, Mesmer?

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: I think you might like it here after all. Think of it as a paid vacation.

items.speaker: Mesmer Jr.
items.text: I won't deny the appeal.

items.speaker: Mesmer Jr.
items.text: But since I'm here with you two, I'd call this a business trip at best.

items.speaker: X
items.text: I propose we look at it as an academic exchange, the kind with complimentary refreshments, featuring the illustrious Dr. Vertin, Dr. Mesmer Jr., and Dr. X.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: I think I'm the only one that feels out of place here, "Doctors."

items.speaker: X
items.text: Ah, well, here's to a pleasant trip.
